Exponential integrals

Source: R/expint.R
exponential-integrals.Rd

  • sc_exp1(): \(E_1(z) = \int_1^\infty e^{-zt} / t \, dt\), complex, with a branch cut on the negative real axis.

  • sc_expi(): \(\mathrm{Ei}(x)\), complex.

  • sc_expn(): the generalised \(E_n(x)\) for whole n.

Usage

sc_exp1(z)

sc_expi(x)

sc_expn(n, x)

Arguments

z

Numeric or complex vector.

x

Numeric vector; in sc_expi(), also complex.

n

Whole numbers within integer range. NaN gives NaN, as in SciPy. A non-whole n is an error: SciPy truncates it with a warning, and zuspecial refuses it so that a fractional order cannot slip through.

Value

A double vector, or a complex vector for complex input.

Details

Arguments are recycled, NA gives NA, and the result takes its dimensions, or else its names, from the arguments as base R arithmetic does; see sc_seterr() for the conditions the kernels raise.

Windows

R on Windows is built with Rtools, whose C library (mingw-w64 v11) evaluates sin() and cos() inaccurately for arguments beyond about 1e5, as base R's own sin() shows there. Complex arguments with a part that large, and real ones where the kernel takes a sine of such a value, are correspondingly inaccurate on Windows only.

See also

https://docs.scipy.org/doc/scipy/reference/special.html#other-special-functions

Examples

sc_exp1(c(0.5, 1, 2))
#> [1] 0.55977359 0.21938393 0.04890051
sc_expi(-1 + 0i)
#> [1] -0.2193839+0i
sc_expn(2, 1)
#> [1] 0.1484955
